answer.rationale: Competitor's price cut creates urgency, but memory_73 clearly shows that targeted discounting on SMB produces -12% retention at renewal—precisely the opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is therefore contraindicated despite leadership pressure. Instead, we have three durable signals: activation messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and moved accounts to first meaningful action; simplified onboarding (memory_31, memory_86) lifted early adoption and completion rates; and referral incentives (memory_57) added qualified revenue from established customers. For price-sensitive churn risk, the optimal play is to deepen product engagement in at-risk accounts (activation_messaging) while simultaneously working to convert established customers into advocates (referral_incentive as secondary lever). Activation messaging addresses the root problem—many churn conversations reflect accounts that haven't yet realized product value—and carries no renewal-cohort penalty. A standard experiment on at-risk SMB cohorts with reinforced activation messaging (in-product prompts, value-unlock sequences) preserves optionality without committing to destructive discounting. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is valid but slower and resource-intensive; referral incentives work on warm existing base, not urgent churn defense. Activation messaging is the fastest, lowest-risk lever that aligns with long-term unit economics.
